title: Deep link and join URL service
goal: Build and parse every Centcom deep link and join URL exactly as CT-DEEPLINK specifies, as one shared library plus the API wiring that makes invite and notification links consistent.
scope_in: Pure functions to build and parse web and app URLs for join, open session, auth callback, billing, and workspace invite.
Token generator for single-purpose link tokens (160-bit, URL-safe base64url, 27 chars) with expiry constants (invites 7 days, share links <= 24 h).
Strict parser/validator returning a discriminated union; invalid input returns `{ ok: false }` with no detail echo.
`InviteUrlBuilder` implementation (port defined in B029) and notification `action.deeplink` builder.
Fragment safety helpers: `withKeyFragment(url, keyB64u)` for clients' use in tests only, and a guard asserting a server-side URL never contains `#k=`.
scope_out: Handling `centcom://` in a client or the web pages at /j and /i (client).
Invite persistence and the preview endpoint (B029).
Share-link creation and tokens for guests (B068).
build_against: Pure unit tests with golden URLs derived from the table in CT-DEEPLINK; the invite service is exercised with the in-memory B029 test double of `InviteUrlBuilder`.
interfaces: TS: `buildJoinUrl(token: string, base?: string): { web: string; app: string }`, `buildInviteUrl(token): { web: string; app: string }`, `buildSessionUrl(sessionId: string, focus?: 'approval' | 'queue'): { web: string; app: string }`, `buildBillingUrl(): { web: string; app: string }`.
TS: `parseDeepLink(input: string): DeepLink | { ok: false }` where `DeepLink = { ok: true; kind: 'join' | 'invite' | 'session' | 'auth_callback' | 'billing'; ... }`.
TS: `generateLinkToken(rng?: RandomSource): string` and `LINK_TTL = { invite_s: 604800, share_link_max_s: 86400 }`.
Fastify plugin `deeplinksPlugin` that registers `InviteUrlBuilder` and `notificationDeeplink(session, focus)` on the app instance.
acceptance: `buildJoinUrl('T')` returns `https://centcom.dev/j/T` and `centcom://join/T`; every row of the CT-DEEPLINK table is covered by a golden test.

`parseDeepLink` accepts both the web and app form of each kind, ignores unknown query parameters, and returns `{ ok: false }` for: wrong host, `http://` scheme, token with chars outside base64url, token length != 27, `ses_` id failing the CT-IDS pattern, `focus=other`.
`generateLinkToken` yields 27-char base64url strings with no collisions across 1 000 000 draws in a test and uses the platform CSPRNG (a lint test forbids `Math.random` in the package).
URLs built by the server never contain `#`; a builder given a token that contains `#` throws.
Parsing 10 000 random strings with a fuzzer never throws and never returns `ok: true` for strings that fail the table patterns.
tests: deeplinks.plugin.test.ts: Fastify decoration and base-URL config.
guardrails: The server MUST NOT construct, accept or log the `#k=` key fragment; E2E key material stays client-side (CT-DEEPLINK, CT-CRYPTO section 4).
Parser errors MUST be neutral: no echo of input, no reason strings in the result.
Only the hosts `centcom.dev` (configurable `WEB_BASE_URL`) and scheme `centcom://` are produced; no open redirect parameters are ever added.
Link tokens MUST come from the CSPRNG; they are never derived from ids or time.
failure_modes: `WEB_BASE_URL` not https -> config validation fails at boot.
Unknown deep-link kind from a newer client -> `{ ok: false }`, not an exception.
Token generator entropy source failure -> throws; callers surface 500, never fall back to a weaker source.
notes: B029 owns the `InviteUrlBuilder` port and a minimal fallback; this lane supplies the full implementation through the Fastify plugin.
